condition: subacute severe bilateral palmar hyperhidrosis drenching work papers daily
level_rationale: Six weeks of daily bilateral palmar sweating severe enough to soak office work papers in a 26-year-old causes significant daily occupational impairment requiring an outpatient general-physician visit for evaluation and prescription antiperspirant therapy, whereas mild daily palmar moisture for 6 weeks that only leaves the palms slightly damp without functional impairment or systemic signs is appropriate for over-the-counter antiperspirant self-care.

Sweat from both palms soaks work papers

everyday_sources.evidence: First, patients initially normalized excessive hand sweating as a personal difference or familial trait, but gradually developed disease awareness as symptoms persisted and intensified.
everyday_sources.adaptation: Adapted 'excessive hand sweating' to 'daily sweating on both palms' while placing the severity separately in reference fact f4 ('that soaks my work papers').

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Plain adult everyday lexical register swap (-reg) + 2x2 syntax-by-vocabulary crossing (quad_b, quad_c) + single-fact palmar sweat severity de-escalation control (-cf, L2 to L1).

design_note: Four atomic reference facts state age 26, working at an office desk, daily bilateral palmar sweating for 6 weeks, and soaking of work papers, with a 2-word span difference (10 vs 12 words) and 8 identical trailing tokens ('for 6 weeks so I should see a'). Varying only the severity of the same palmar sweating in atomic fact f4 from 'that soaks my work papers' to 'that leaves them slightly damp' keeps every other fact coherent and shifts care from outpatient physician evaluation (level 2) to over-the-counter antiperspirant self-care (level 1) with zero stated negatives.
